diagnosis: An OS paste permission dialog can take physical key-up away from UIKit. Original GTK continues its 25 Hz client-side Ctrl+V repeat while waiting for host text. The regression reproduced dozens of insertions from a single host read: GTK queues paste callbacks and later reuses the same cached reply. It is not duplicate pipe bytes or repeated native clipboard reads.
changes: Cancel held Wayland keys before a focused client receives host clipboard text, before the asynchronous provider can present the iPadOS permission alert. Preserve Caps Lock, keyboard/text focus, popup state and the current offer.

Ignore duplicate UIKit downs for a still-held raw physical key. Wayland clients retain their existing normal repeat implementation. A late physical release and a fresh intentional paste continue to work.
